No. The land-change method could not evaluate this property (ASSET-J). The zonal statistics step returned an error: the source coverage the asset needs had not been prepared, so no observation was made. The run metadata also lists no asset area (null).

This means there are no results at all, not even a "no change detected" result. You can't read it as evidence that the property is free of land change or deforestation after the 2020-12-31 baseline.

The run on 2026-11-12 used TerraUY land-change, an early-access version (land-change/1). It was set up to use Hansen/UMD Global Forest Change and the JRC 2020 forest cover reference. Neither dataset produced an observation for this asset.

To get an assessment, the missing source coverage would need to be prepared and the analysis re-run.
